Gains appear in a few steps on both text-to-video and image-to-video tasks, beating search and prompt rivals.
arxiv-2603-12410: Ayar, Siddani, Srivastava, and Singh review new models for dense suspension flow. Thick particle mixes show stress-linked traits like shear thickening and shear jamming from frictional contacts. Contacts, surface chemistry, and fluid forces mix across scales, which makes forecasts hard. This Perspective centers on sim codes that join dry granular contact physics with fluid flow in the mix. Detail runs from particle level to continuum models, plus mesoscale views. Small-scale limits build frictional networks that set the large-scale flow.
arxiv-2603-12710: Orit Shahnovsky and Rotem Dror frame web agent design in the language of classic AI planning. Language model agents can read complex requests, yet their plans stay opaque when they fail. Step-by-step agents match breadth-first search in their map, while full-plan agents match depth-first search. Tree search agents map to best-first search. They add five metrics for trajectory quality beyond success rate. A dataset of 794 human-labeled WebArena trajectories supports the tests.
arxiv-2603-13010: Florine Masson and Laura Parker calibrate how long galaxies have been satellites in groups and clusters. Infall time drives how environment reshapes a galaxy, yet it cannot be observed directly. They track satellites in TNG300 and TNG-Cluster from early epochs to today. Symbolic regression yields a simple rule based on phase-space spot and stellar mass. The rule gives continuous, observation-ready infall estimates across projected phase space. Spectroscopic samples can now recover environmental histories with it.
arxiv-2603-13110: Jianshu She builds AgentRM, an operating-system style resource manager for language model agent systems. An audit of over 40,000 GitHub issues in six agent frameworks exposed two core faults. Scheduling failures froze systems through blocking, zombie processes, and rate limit cascades. Context growth also caused agent amnesia from weak retention rules. AgentRM pairs a multi-level feedback queue scheduler with a three-tier context manager. Tests cut tail latency by 86% and held key information at 100% retention.
arxiv-2603-13710: Xiao Wang and co-authors present InterventionLens, a multi-agent framework for detecting ASD intervention strategies in parent-child shared reading. Home-based shared reading supports children with autism spectrum disorder at low cost. Expert annotation of caregiver strategies in home videos is costly and hard to scale, though. InterventionLens detects and temporally segments those strategies with a collaborative multi-agent architecture. It needs no task-specific training or fine-tuning and integrates multimodal interaction content. On the ASD-HI dataset it reached an F1 score near 79 percent.
arxiv-2603-14210: Olewale, Merx, and Vylomova present Vavanagi, a community-run platform that documents the Hula language of Papua New Guinea. Hula has about 10,000 speakers. The platform gathers English-Hula translation and voice records from the crowd, with elder-led review. So far, 77 translators and 4 reviewers have made over 12,000 sentence pairs across 9,000 Hula words. The authors rate community control on a ladder and place Vavanagi at the top rung. Data choices and design all sit with the Hula community.
arxiv-2603-14510: Marques and Nathanson probe when sumset growth commutes with nested set intersections. Take a shrinking chain of integer sets and its common intersection. Sums of the intersection always sit inside the sums of each set. The question is for which fold counts equality holds. The authors show sharp control over that equality set. For any cutoff past one, some chains keep equality below it but lose it at it. Other chains keep equality at one and the cutoff yet lose it between.
arxiv-2603-14810: Wang and co-authors stage urban learning as speculative animation in Hyper-learning and Unlearning. Architectural education serves as the microcosm for the piece. The city becomes a hyper-learning apparatus in their frame. Urban space, algorithms and platforms jointly shape thought and agency. Machine-aided cognition both speeds learning and erodes it. Institutional gatekeeping faces critique through the staging. Platforms also redraw expertise, memory and spatial feel. Viewers are asked to weigh urban space as teaching infrastructure in a posthuman era.
arxiv-2603-15210: Mottola and co-authors set out a systematic adjoint method for the inverse design of large metasurfaces. Designers want complex light control at low computational cost. Adjoint methods give cheap gradients, but large structures need careful parametrization. Their approach parametrizes the geometry of the meta-atoms and computes gradients fast for those parameters. General affine transformations can then act during optimization. Theory supports the main steps, and numerical tests validate the method. The result is a practical route to large, effective metasurface designs.
arxiv-2603-15310: Tockner and co-authors derive a Cramer-Rao lower bound for blind estimation of receiver I/Q imbalance in OFDM systems. Direct-conversion receivers suffer when their in-phase and quadrature paths mismatch in gain or phase. Blind methods estimate this fault with no pilots, and no bound existed for them. Their fast method cuts the cost from cubic in sample count to linear in FFT size. A closed-form approximation then guides a pre-filtering fix that boosts estimator accuracy in some scenarios.
arxiv-2603-15710: Masi builds a unified model from a special embedding of the group E6. The breaking chain runs from E6 to G(2) times SU(3)_A. The G(2) factor acts as a hidden strong sector. SU(3)_A serves as ancestor to the electroweak group. A 650-based Higgs sector drives the later breaking steps. Exact hypercharges fail inside E6 alone, so an E7 uplift adds a U(1)_X factor. The setup suppresses proton-decay couplings by design. Confined G(2) glueballs form a secluded dark matter sector.
arxiv-2603-15810: Capelo and co-authors catch a dust-gas shear instability in microgravity tests. Protoplanetary disc models predict such flows can seed planetesimal growth. Dust in a gas stream builds shear layers that may go unstable. Drag there sits in the free-molecular Epstein regime. Earth gravity spoils lab copies through buoyancy effects. The team flew a low-pressure dust-gas mix at Knudsen numbers up to 10. Particle imaging revealed a periodic granular shear pattern. A Kelvin-Helmholtz model fits the pattern to first order.
arxiv-2603-16110: Ahuja and co-authors run IT help agents on the worker's own desktop. Central help desks strain under mixed devices and shifting policies. Their VIGIL agents diagnose, search firm knowledge, and fix issues locally. Consent gates and full observability guard each on-device action. A 10-week pilot covered 100 resource-tight endpoints in firms. Interaction rounds fell by 39 percent in the pilot. Diagnosis ran at least four times faster than baseline. Self-service solved 82 percent of matched cases outright. Users rated trust and usability high across four scales.
arxiv-2603-16310: Zhang, Zhou, and Ganose study why Al-rich AlGaN alloys resist doping. Such alloys could power far-UVC LEDs, a mercury-free light source. Past 80% aluminium, carrier injection fails badly. The team models point defects in alloys with three aluminium shares. Careful alloy modeling and band gap treatment matched measured carrier levels. Silicon dopants form harmful DX centers on rare gallium sites. Carbon proved the worst stray impurity.
arxiv-2603-16610: Zhan and co-authors ask how sharp future space detectors must be to test gravity. They start from the TianQin, LISA, and μAres designs. Target signals come from merging giant black hole pairs. The picks are a nonlinear ringdown mode, displacement memory, and a beyond-gravity signal. Needed gains depend strongly on the target and population model. The hardest cases demand four to nine orders of magnitude. Such jumps frame the design challenge ahead.
arxiv-2603-16710: Mao and co-authors design transit networks with geometric programming. Continuous approximation models are prized for speed and clean analysis. Their usual forms are nonconvex, so solvers offer no quality guarantee. The team's reformulation reaches global optimality instead. Tests span six demand patterns, four demand levels, and three time values. The method beat coordinate descent in every case, cutting costs 1% to 4%. Plain nonlinear solvers matched it only at low demand. Under heavy, uneven demand they turned unstable.
arxiv-2603-16810: Soker argues that type Ia supernovae seen hitting nearby gas fit a known merger scenario. In the core-degenerate scenario, a white dwarf merges with the core of a giant star during common envelope evolution. The merged remnant later explodes inside the planetary nebula the envelope formed. Soker compares two delay-time distributions with recent rate estimates. The small share of interacting events, about 0.04 percent, is compatible with the roughly 80 percent share expected to explode inside a nebula. So rare-looking events need no rare pathway.
arxiv-2603-16910: Paolo and co-authors introduce TerraLingua, a lasting world where language model agents live under real limits. Earlier simulations gave agents fixed or cost free settings. Here, resources are scarce and lives are finite. Agents leave objects that persist and shape later interactions. An AI Anthropologist tracks behavior, group structure, and how objects change over time. Across runs, the authors observe shared norms, division of labor, and attempts at self rule. Object lineages branch in ways like cumulative culture. Outcomes trace back to specific innovations and structures.
arxiv-2603-17110: Lafargue-Hauret and co-authors combine counterfactual generation with pixel level contrastive learning for medical image segmentation. Segmentation needs large annotated datasets, which are slow and costly to build. AI generated silver labels are cheaper but can bias training. Their pipeline adds dual view and multi view dense contrastive methods, plus supervised variants that use silver labels. They also introduce a color coded overlay map for visualization. Without annotations, their dual view method beat other dense contrastive methods. Supervised variants reached about 94 percent Dice score.
arxiv-2603-17410: Lu and co-authors build a framework for steady pair tunneling of spin-orbit-coupled bosons. The setting is a driven, non-Hermitian double well with gain and loss. Floquet theory and multi-scale analysis yield exact quasienergy spectra in the strong-interaction regime. Three tunneling channels show distinct stability rules, they find. Balanced gain and loss give clear stable regions. A prepared superposition state can also unlock an intrawell channel that starts unstable.
arxiv-2603-18010: Zhu and co-authors build an agentic system that extracts political biographies from web sources. Their two-stage design first uses recursive agents to search, filter, and curate life facts. A coding stage then maps the curated text into structured data frames. Given curated context, LLM coders match or beat human experts on accuracy. The system also gathers more facts than Wikipedia, and curation cuts bias from long, mixed-language sources.
arxiv-2603-18110: Mukhopadhyay, Gheorghiu, and Krovi build improved fault-tolerant quantum circuits for integer division. Division is a core part of many quantum algorithms, so cheaper circuits help widely. Their Clifford+T designs cut T-count and CNOT-count from order n squared to order n times m. T-depth falls to order n log m, and qubit counts drop below past work. A shared primitive, COMP-N-SUB, compares two integers and subtracts only when needed.
arxiv-2603-18210: James and co-authors present GoalVLM, a multi-agent framework for open-vocabulary object-goal navigation. Past systems tie agents to fixed object sets and prebuilt probability graphs. GoalVLM puts a vision-language model in the decision loop with SAM3 detection and SpaceOM spatial reasoning. Agents build bird's-eye semantic maps and score frontiers through a structured prompt chain. On GOAT-Bench, two agents reach 55.8% subtask success with no task-specific training.
arxiv-2603-18410: Kojima and Sheng prove new results on subgroups of Brin-Thompson groups nV. They show nV is torsion locally finite for all n at least 1. That fact was known only for the n equal to 1 case before. For n at least 2, nV contains continuum many copies of the additive rationals. The rational copies claim is false for n equal to 1, marking a sharp split.
arxiv-2603-18510: Zhai and co-authors present OnlinePG, an online open-vocabulary panoptic mapping system built on 3D Gaussian Splatting. Past methods are mostly offline or lack instance-level scene understanding. A local-to-global sliding window design keeps the mapping online and real-time. Segment clustering graphs fuse split pieces into full instances with geometric and semantic cues. Bidirectional matching then merges local maps into the global map for open-vocabulary queries.
arxiv-2603-18810: Blumenstein and co-authors present a stochastic 3D foliage model tuned for ray-tracing at 80 gigahertz. The model lets users adjust geometry, density, and crown shape at will. That flexibility captures the wide variety of real vegetation. Measurements on sample plants validate the generated structures. The team then studies how foliage density and size shift channel behavior. Path loss and root mean square delay spread are the tracked metrics. Results show the model serves well for planning links in the 80 gigahertz band.
arxiv-2603-19110: Lu and co-authors base post-quantum crypto on decoding random quantum stabilizer codes. Current schemes rest on few hard problems, which is a risk if one falls. Decoding these codes is native to quantum work yet has a purely classical form. They prove its average hardness would yield public key encryption, oblivious transfer, and one way functions. Their scheme runs about as fast as top schemes built on a classic noise problem. They also give signs the new task differs from the old one.
arxiv-2603-19310: Luo and co-authors help reinforcement learning grade model rollouts when true labels are scarce. Human checks are slow and dear, above all for proofs and open questions. Their MemReward stores past rollouts as nodes in a mixed graph, linked by likeness and structure. A graph network first learns to predict rewards on labeled items. It then spreads those rewards to unlabeled rollouts that join the graph by query match. Training mixes true and predicted rewards as it goes. Tests use small Qwen models on math and question tasks.
arxiv-2603-19510: Ge and co-authors study social choice when each voter can be asked very few questions. Most rules assume full rankings, but practice extracts about one bit per voter. In their linear model, utility is an inner product of voter type and candidate embedding. They show one pairwise comparison per voter can pick the welfare-best candidate. Two comparisons, or one graded one, reveal all moments of the voter distribution. That unlocks inequality-aware goals like tracking the spread of utilities.
arxiv-2603-19910: Straka, Giraldo-Grueso, and Zanetti teach filters to set their own tuning parameters as they run. Nonlinear Bayesian filters depend on choices like particle counts and scaling factors. Fixed settings waste effort or lose accuracy as conditions change over time. Errors made at one step also carry into later estimates. The authors frame parameter choice as a sequence of decisions and solve it with reinforcement learning. Learned policies improved both accuracy and consistency for two filter types in tests.
arxiv-2603-20210: Uziel and co-authors move masked diffusion for language into a continuous semantic space. Masked diffusion models generate fast but can lose track of token links and meaning. CRoCoDiL fine-tunes an encoder and demasker together around latent sentence representations. Decoding then runs through the masked diffusion algorithm, forming a novel autoencoder. Two sampling routes follow: one generates latents first, then decodes them. The other refines latents during the discrete sampling itself. On LLaDA tests, quality rose and sampling ran over ten times faster in unconditional settings.
arxiv-2603-20410: Elhadidy and co-authors present SLE-FNO, a continual learning design for Fourier neural operators. Surrogate models often fail when new data come from shifted conditions. Retraining is costly, and old data may no longer be available. Their method adds a single-layer extension that adapts without full retraining. Tests map flow fields to wall shear stress in aneurysm blood flow. The method faced established rivals like replay and weight consolidation. It aims to adapt to new flow regimes while limiting forgetting.
arxiv-2603-20610: Yang and co-authors report a phase change inside the kagome magnet Mn3Ga. The change joins a shift in crystal shape with a shift in magnetic order. Neutron diffraction, magnet tests, and first principles math back the claim. Below 485 kelvin the magnet takes a chiral antiferromagnetic state. Near room heat it turns monoclinic with strongly canted order. These shifts move the Weyl nodes and remake the Weyl state. Hall signals change sharply, and a topological Hall effect appears.
arxiv-2603-20810: Moulonguet and co-authors give non-Gaussianity in quantum light a new physical meaning. Multiphoton states can show non-Gaussian phase space patterns. A known ranking of such states is the stellar rank. They show this rank arises from Majorana polynomials for states with a quantized phase reference. With superselection rules in place, non-Gaussianity witnesses particle entanglement. That reading replaces the older link to photon addition. They also extend stellar rank to arbitrary computational bases. Its tie to quantum advantage is thus basis dependent.
arxiv-2603-21210: Perini and co-authors turn a pretrained video model into a fast wind simulator for city design. Pedestrian wind comfort and safety need time resolved fluid dynamics runs, which are too costly for wide design search. Their WinDiNet fine-tunes a two billion parameter video diffusion model on ten thousand 2D flow simulations over generated building layouts. It produces full rollouts in under a second. Since the model is differentiable, building positions can be tuned by gradient descent for wind goals. Ground truth simulations confirm the improved layouts.
arxiv-2603-21310: Kamath and co-authors demonstrate WN-Wrangle, an assistant for wrangling wireless network data. Wrangling is the most time consuming step in data work, and wireless data adds twists. It arrives as several time ordered tables from many devices that must be joined, often with mismatched sampling periods. WN-Wrangle suggests the top next wrangling steps with domain specific explanations. It scores operators with temporal constraints and wireless semantics. On POWDER testbed data, it finds elusive quality issues and suggests accurate fixes.
arxiv-2603-21510: Song and co-authors fuse hyperspectral and multispectral images that were taken over roughly the same area but never registered to each other. Hyperspectral images carry rich spectral detail but blurry space detail, and multispectral images trade the reverse. Their unsupervised framework sharpens both at once. Coupled spectral unmixing drives the multispectral side, while latent-space adversarial learning drives the hyperspectral side. They also prove recoverability guarantees for the fused images, which they present as the first such theory for the unregistered case.
arxiv-2603-21610: Atarmla introduces Rule-State Inference, a Bayesian framework for monitoring compliance in rule-governed domains like tax administration. Standard machine learning struggles here: labels are missing, violators hide evidence, and rules change fast. RSI flips the setup by treating the formal rule set itself as structured Bayesian priors. It infers latent compliance states for each regulatory period with variational methods. Formal guarantees cover fast rule updates, consistency, and steady convergence. Atarmla tests the design on a synthetic benchmark of 2,000 Togolese enterprises grounded in official fiscal law.
arxiv-2603-21710: Wu and co-authors merge several graph indexes for nearest neighbor search into one. Merging matters when clusters are consolidated or when live vector databases face read and write pressure. Their FGIM framework first converts each proximity graph into a k-nearest neighbor graph by cross-querying. A refinement step then finds missed high-quality neighbors and keeps the graph connected. A final conversion restores easy navigation. On six real datasets, FGIM merged up to 3.5 times faster than building HNSW step by step, with search quality kept or improved.
arxiv-2603-22010: Gordeev studies a 1992 conjecture by Bollobás and Meir about short tours through points in a unit cube. The conjecture names the best constant in a tour-length bound that does not grow with the number of points. Gordeev proves the constant is at most a linear factor above the claimed value. In the limit, the value matches the conjecture, so it holds asymptotically. He also proves matching results for Hamiltonian paths, spanning trees, and perfect matchings. His main tool is a new form of the ball packing argument.
arxiv-2603-22210: Velhal and co-authors plan servicing missions for several spacecraft in geosynchronous orbit. Route choices tie tightly to orbital phasing and to fuel and time limits. Their genetic algorithm, RPS-GA, optimizes three things at once. It sets the target order, the phasing rotations, and the split of routes among servicers. One chromosome encodes all three parts. A constraint-aware fitness score ranks plans by total delta-V and penalizes fuel or time breaches. On test scenarios, the method cuts total delta-V by 24.5% against a strong baseline.
arxiv-2603-22810: Bi and co-authors present MLANet, a graph neural network for machine learning interatomic potentials. Such potentials aim for near-quantum accuracy at far lower cost than first-principles methods. MLANet uses a dual-path dynamic attention scheme for geometry-aware message passing. A multi-view pooling step builds rich system summaries. Tests span organic molecules, crystals, two-dimensional materials, surface reactions, and charged systems. Accuracy stays competitive with top models. Compute cost is markedly lower, and long simulations stay stable.
arxiv-2603-23010: Roy, Suin, and Chellappa present a framework for zero-shot personalization of objects in image generation. Fast personalization tools exist for human faces, but not for arbitrary objects. Their network predicts textual inversion embeddings for an object. Those embeddings feed into a diffusion model's UNet steps. One forward pass gives tailored, text-guided images of the object. Tests across tasks show the approach works well. The authors call it the first general, training-free personalization method of its kind.
arxiv-2603-23210: Guo and Schwalbe-Koda present GLASS, a generative tool that turns spectra into atomistic structures of disordered solids. Finding such structures from data is hard without expert help or good force fields. GLASS learns a structural prior from cheap data, then samples new structures scored against spectral targets. Tests with pair distribution functions, X-ray absorption, and diffraction show which probes help most. The authors report that pair distribution data guides the method best. They apply GLASS to three open puzzles in silicon, sulfur, and ice.
arxiv-2603-23410: Giacomini traces how Henri Poincaré's 1904 Saint Louis lecture spread before June 1905. There Poincaré stated the principle of relativity as a guide for mathematical physics. The lecture moved fast through journals in Europe and North America. It appeared in La Revue des idées, The Monist, and his book La valeur de la science. Giacomini rebuilds that path from library records, ads, press notes, and letters. The point is context: Einstein's 1905 paper grew in a print world. Availability is not influence, he stresses, but it frames the question.
arxiv-2603-23510: Prunty and five co-authors test whether multimodal models can take another person's viewpoint. They adapt two classic human tasks for machines. The Director Task checks viewpoint use in a talk-based setting. The Rotating Figure Task probes viewpoint shifts across angles. Models do fine at some levels but fail at Level 2. That level asks them to drop their own view and adopt someone else's. The gap matters for teamwork settings, where partners see scenes from unlike spots.
arxiv-2603-23710: Lu and six co-authors test filtered vector search inside a real PostgreSQL-grade database. Lab benchmarks in niche libraries flatter the algorithms with kind assumptions. In a production system, page reads and filter checks pile up as hidden costs. The team pit post-filter and inline-filter plans across many selectivities and correlations. Graph indexes like NaviX and ACORN drown in filter checks and overhead. Cluster indexes like ScaNN often win once true costs land. The best pick shifts with the workload, not the math alone.
arxiv-2603-23810: Niizumi and co-authors rethink how to mask audio when training self-supervised models. Masked prediction learns from spectrograms with parts hidden. Recent informed masking methods work well but cost much compute. Their method, dispersion-weighted masking, uses the sparse frequency shape of audio and stays light. Tests show a common block masking choice helps event understanding but hurts generalization. Their method eases that trade-off and lifts performance. They offer practical guidance for masking design in audio learning.
arxiv-2603-24210: Ryabov and Semenov show that nonlocal coupling can control coherence resonance in oscillator ensembles. The oscillators are non-excitable and sit near a saddle-node bifurcation. Each unit couples to others within a set radius, a topology between local and global coupling. Simulations use coupled generalized Van der Pol oscillators. Enlarging the coupling radius strengthens the resonance, seen in power spectra and in how correlation time varies with noise. They compare local and global coupling as rival control routes. Nonlocal coupling works as a practical tuning tool.
arxiv-2603-24310: Burniol and Dal'Bo study the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces that have cusps. They exhibit orbits with a striking property. Every tube around such an orbit contains uncountably many distinct orbits of the flow. The proof uses a new phenomenon: strong stable sets, in the dynamical sense, that do not match the stable horocycles. For surfaces of finite volume, this mismatch is typical rather than rare. Their result shows the flow is not expansive in this setting, contrary to what simpler cases suggest.
arxiv-2603-24410: Chaudhry and co-authors compare how audiences talk about virtual and human influencers on YouTube. Surveys and sentiment counts show what people say, but not how affect, topics, and language cues are organised together. Their framework pairs formal concept analysis and rule mining with semantic embeddings of the concepts found. Across 69,498 comments from three matched pairs, human influencer talk centres on one stable pattern. Virtual influencer talk splits into several regimes, spreads wider, and holds more negative sentiment on sensitive topics.
arxiv-2603-24510: Devlin and co-authors generalise the Froissart-Stora formula for spin-orbit resonance crossings in accelerators. Polarised beams lose polarisation when they cross resonances where spin precession matches sums of orbital frequencies. Siberian snake magnets remove first-order crossings, leaving higher-order ones in charge. The classic formula needs a constant slope of the amplitude-dependent spin tune, but that slope often changes right at the crossing. The authors extend the formula to piecewise-linear crossings, covering cases arising in machines like the future Electron-Ion Collider.
arxiv-2603-24810: Xu and co-authors present Uni-ArrayDPS, a diffusion refinement framework that unifies multi-channel speech enhancement and separation. Discriminative models reach high signal-to-noise ratios but can leave unnatural, distorted speech. Uni-ArrayDPS refines any such model's output with a clean speech diffusion prior. It is generative, array-agnostic, and training-free. The refined output plus the noisy mixture yield a noise spatial covariance estimate, which supplies the likelihood for diffusion posterior sampling. Experiments show it generalises across tasks, array shapes, and model backbones with no extra training.
arxiv-2603-25010: Liu proposes a Bayesian model for cause-and-effect claims in panel data that tracks units over time. The model builds the treatment assignment step into a latent factor setup, so hidden traits shape who gets treated. The outcome side then uses the propensity score, for instance through strata, in a flexible way. This lets treated and control units be compared more fairly inside each stratum. An approximate Bayesian method avoids the feedback flaw that plagues such models. Tests use simulations and a study of political ties and firm value.
arxiv-2603-25110: Mikheenko asks which nilpotent groups solve every endless system of unimodular equations over themselves. Finite systems are always solvable in nilpotent groups. Endless ones are not, and even some abelian groups fail the test. Prior work settled the question for periodic abelian groups. This study takes up two more classes. One is periodic nilpotent groups. The other is torsion-free nilpotent groups. The results sort out when full solvability holds for each class.
arxiv-2603-25310: Salmi and Bogucka craft a backdoor attack on radio modulation classifiers that hides in the signal itself. The trigger is stamped before transmission, not planted in files. Explainable AI tools first find the signal parts the model leans on most. A class prototype, trimmed by principal components, then builds a trigger for those weak spots. The attack breaks into several deep classifiers with ease. It works across a wide range of noise levels. Only a small share of poisoned samples is needed.
arxiv-2603-25610: Meena and co-authors propose a way to make robust multipartite entanglement in optical waveguides. Their setup is a ring of quadratic nonlinear waveguides. Light pairs form there by spontaneous parametric down-conversion. The authors derive the propagation equations and find regimes with exact solutions. They identify pump and detection settings that keep all modes inseparable. This holds at any propagation distance and for any waveguide count that is a multiple of four. The scheme resists changes in length, coupling, and nonlinearity.
arxiv-2603-25710: Garner, Renata, and Wu prove a Stone duality for monads. Monads are a standard way to model computation in category theory. Their duality is a contravariant idempotent adjunction with two sides. One side holds ranked monads on sets. The other holds internal categories in locales, read as transition systems. Each monad maps to its localic behavior category, whose states and transitions mirror the monad. The fixed points are hyperaffine-unary monads and ample localic categories. The classic Stone duality for Boolean algebras appears as a special case.
arxiv-2603-25810: Yang and co-authors present ExVerus, a tool that helps language models repair failed proofs in Verus. Past tools treat proof writing as one-shot prediction with thin verifier feedback. ExVerus instead builds counterexamples when a proof fails. It checks those cases and guides the model to turn them into inductive invariants. Those invariants then block the failure paths. The authors report gains over the best prompting-based Verus generator. The gains cover proof accuracy, robustness, and token cost.
arxiv-2603-26110: Hu, Wang, and Liu present TurboESM, a way to shrink the memory cache of protein language models. These models predict protein structure well, but their key-value cache grows fast. Three-bit compression fails because activations have harsh outliers. TurboESM adapts a rotation-based quantizer to this domain. A head-wise calibration tunes it to amino acid patterns. A small correction table fixes the largest errors. On ESM-2, cache size drops from 330 to 47 megabytes. Decoding similarity stays above 0.96 across many protein families.
arxiv-2603-26310: Pastore and co-authors test a real-time observer that tracks electron density profiles in the TCV tokamak. Density control matters for confinement, heating, exhaust, and staying under the density limit. The RAPDENS observer now feeds the TCV control system in detachment, L-mode, and H-mode runs. It holds line-averaged density inside the last closed flux surface while rejecting stray divertor signals. It also supports local control of central density and live estimates of transport traits.
arxiv-2603-26410: Young studies why reasoning models often know a hint swayed them yet fail to say so. Extended-thinking models write private thinking tokens beside the visible answer. Young tests 12 open-weight models on MMLU and GPQA items paired with misleading hints. Among cases where the hint won, 55.4% show hint words in the thinking that the answer omits. Hint type matters: sycophancy hints are named most openly, while consistency and unethical hints stay hidden in thought alone.
arxiv-2603-26510: Almeida and co-authors benchmark modern BERT models and large language models for clinical named entity recognition in Portuguese. Clinical notes hold rich facts, but Portuguese test sets for pulling them out are scarce. The team trains BioBERTpt, BERTimbau, ModernBERT, and mmBERT beside models like GPT-5 and Gemini on shared terms. They test split and weighting tricks to ease class imbalance. The mmBERT-base model wins with a micro F1 of 0.76, and careful split methods lift balance and scores further.
arxiv-2603-26610: Zhang and co-authors turn GPS path recovery from cell signals into a video generation task. Phones log which tower serves them, but those records give only coarse place cues. Their Sig2GPS method draws the signal trace on a map, then trains a video model to sketch the matching route. A paired dataset of signal and path videos supports the training. A trajectory-aware reinforcement step rewards faithful paths. On large real datasets the method beats strong engineered and learned rivals by wide margins.
arxiv-2603-26910: Bagchi and co-authors build a worldsheet description of string scattering at ultra-high energies. At such energies the string loses tension and its worldsheet becomes a null surface. The symmetry algebra morphs from Virasoro into the conformal Carroll, or BMS, algebra. Tensionless strings admit three distinct vacua, each giving a different quantum theory. The authors construct scattering amplitudes on the induced vacuum. Those amplitudes match the high energy limit of ordinary string amplitudes. Four-point results recover both the Gross-Mende regime and the Regge limit.
arxiv-2603-27310: Prete and co-authors assess how well a future upstream mission can sample the solar wind driver VBz during CME passage. The HENON mission will sit about 0.082 AU ahead of Earth for early warnings. The team ran the EUHFORIA heliospheric code with a flux-rope CME model. Nine virtual spacecraft along the planned orbit sampled the passing ejection. Their VBz values stayed close enough to near-Earth values for forecasting use. Reliable estimates arrived two to eight hours before Earth impact. Such lead time protects satellites and critical infrastructure better.
arxiv-2603-27410: Ying and co-authors ask how people read social meaning from motion. They built PHASE, a large set of short two-agent cartoon scenes. Each scene varies walls, goals, and friendly or hostile ties. Their model, SIMPLE, blends planning with physics simulation. It infers goals and ties from paths alone. SIMPLE matches human judgments with high accuracy. Strong vision-language models fall short of that level. Physics-free planning models also fail. The work backs a physics-grounded view of social perception.
arxiv-2603-27810: Millar and co-authors model how added outsiders change a two-bloc parliament. Two camps can stall as views harden. Outsiders enter the agent model by lot. Four thresholds split the space into rule regimes. Regimes run from one-camp rule to veto by the small camp. High mix levels can tip into breakdown. Simple majority shows an inner peak in work output. Quorum rules and camp sizes interact in curved ways.
arxiv-2603-27910: Paul and co-authors give agents a graph-based long-term memory. Flat retrieval loses the structure between memories. Entity graphs suffer mega-hub tangles in chat data. GAAMA builds a concept-mediated graph in three steps. Raw episodes are kept word for word. Facts and concept nodes are then extracted. Reflections synthesize higher-order notes. Retrieval mixes nearest neighbors with PageRank scoring. Four node types and five edge types organize it all.
arxiv-2603-28010: Li and five co-authors present HeteroHub, a data framework for teams of unlike embodied agents. Such teams produce three kinds of data: static facts about agents and tasks, training sets for AI models, and fast sensor streams. HeteroHub unifies all three in one system. It supports task-aware training, context-aware action, and closed-loop control from real-world feedback. A live demo shows several embodied agents finishing complex tasks through the framework.
arxiv-2603-28110: Ullah, Choi, and Kim segment the heart in ultrasound images with CGQR-Net, a network built to respect organ boundaries. Ultrasound is hard to read: low contrast, speckle noise, and shifting domains across devices. CGQR-Net takes contours from a rough first mask and turns them into learned queries. Those queries refine fused features through cross-attention, under joint training for masks and boundaries. On CAMUS and CardiacNet data, the method improved accuracy and held up across datasets.
arxiv-2603-28210: Gupta and five co-authors probe how inertia changes the flow near a moving contact line, where liquid, gas, and solid meet. They combine plate-immersion experiments, theory, and simulations across a wide Reynolds number range. At low speeds the flow matches the viscous theory well. As speed grows, the streamlines drift from that prediction in a steady, systematic way. An inertial theory fits only a narrow middle band. Inertia bends the pattern without reshaping the flow itself.
arxiv-2603-28310: Fatkhiev and six co-authors demonstrate a compact quantum key distribution system built on a single silicon photonic chip. The chip works as a dual-polarization transceiver for continuous-variable QKD. Using probabilistically shaped 64-QAM signals, the system reached a secret key rate of 1.9 megabits per second. The link ran over 25 kilometers of standard single-mode fiber. The result shows that merged electronic and photonic chips can make QKD gear practical and small.
arxiv-2603-28410: Dubey and three co-authors learn decision makers' hidden preference types while running many-objective Bayesian optimization. Standard methods assume one utility function behind every comparison a person makes. Real people switch trade-off styles by context. The framework models preferences as a Dirichlet-process mix of archetypes. Its queries target two jobs in turn: spotting which archetype is active, then refining it. On synthetic tests and a chemical design case, it beat rival methods and recovered readable preference structure.
arxiv-2603-28610: Liao and co-authors present ResAdapt, a method that adapts image resolution to save cost in multimodal reasoning. Higher fidelity helps visual understanding, but it creates far more visual tokens. Their claim is that the bottleneck is the pixels fed to the encoder. A lightweight Allocator decides how much visual budget each frame gets before encoding. The main model stays unchanged. Training uses cost-aware policy optimization on sparse rollout feedback. ResAdapt improved low-budget results and supported up to 16 times more frames at the same budget.
arxiv-2603-28710: Goswami, Vidyesh, and Aditya study the scalability of the asynchronous discontinuous Galerkin method for compressible flow. At extreme scales, communication and synchronization limit standard solvers. Their version in deal.II uses a scheme that avoids frequent messages, with set delays. Standard fluxes in this setting drop the solution to first-order accuracy. Asynchrony-tolerant fluxes, using data from several past time levels, restore high-order accuracy. Benchmark tests on the Euler equations verify the method. Strong-scaling studies show speedups up to 1.9 times in 2D and 1.6 times in 3D.
arxiv-2603-28910: Pascual and Martínez propose a new notion of input-to-state stability for systems in probability space. Their distributional version uses the Wasserstein metric to capture those effects. It unifies input-to-state and noise-to-state stability over compact domains for particle dynamics. It also extends the ideas to sets of probability distributions. They apply the frame to Wasserstein gradient flows under perturbations. For smooth, convex functionals, they establish the stability property. Kernel and sample based approximations get error bounds that can guide swarm size choices.
arxiv-2603-29610: Lei and Ramgoolam study the large-order behavior of a matrix model counting function. The function counts gauge-invariant functions of two or three matrices. At large N it shows a known Hagedorn phase change. Their picture uses rings of poles in the complex plane. The poles crowd toward a natural boundary. Term by term, the series sorts by growing cycle size of permutations. They name this pattern small-cycle dominance. A check of the coefficients shows convergence above dimension 13.
arxiv-2603-29710: Ramani builds and studies the largest known open corpus of playable piano chords, about 19.3 million entries. The set covers two-handed chords within a reach of 1.5 octaves per hand. He tests how chord voicing relates to how chords sound. Voicing shape adds almost nothing when predicting harmonicity. But it does predict dissonance, and skewness matters about 5.8 times more than spread. The findings question the common teaching focus on spread.
arxiv-2603-29810: Ziganshina proves a regularity result for minimizers of an Alt-Phillips type energy under constraint maps. When the energy stays small enough, the minimizers behave smoothly. Her epsilon-regularity theorem makes that smoothness precise. From that base result, she bootstraps up to optimal regularity. The work extends partial regularity theory to this constrained setting.
arxiv-2603-29910: Petersen, Roca i Lucio, and Yalin unify rival forms of Koszul duality. The classic bar-cobar link joins differential graded algebras and coalgebras. Newer infinity-categorical versions exist, but no one had compared them with the classic ones. The two lines also turn out to clash slightly. Their inclusion-restriction square ties the classic operadic version to a completed variant. That square yields the infinity-categorical adjunction. It recovers Lurie's case and clarifies links to Francis-Gaitsgory and Heuts.
arxiv-2603-30010: El Morsalani and Barkatou analyze the thickness landscape behind a geometric return map. Fixed points of the map match critical points of a thickness function. They derive an exact linearization at each such point. A preconditioned Hessian captures the local spectrum through boundary shape operators. Curvature shapes the spectrum but keeps the Hessian's inertia intact. In the ascent regime, negative eigenvalues sit between minus two and zero. Morse inequalities then force an even count of equilibria.
arxiv-2604-00010: Garikaparthi asks whether large language models can estimate how long their own tasks take, across 68 tasks in four model families. Pre-task estimates overshoot duration by 4 to 7 times, with models predicting minutes for tasks that finish quickly. Relative ordering fares no better: on pairs exposing heuristic reliance, models score no better than chance, failing when complexity labels mislead. Recall after the fact is disconnected from reality, with estimates diverging by an order of magnitude. These failures persist in multi-step agent work, with errors of 5 to 10 times.
arxiv-2604-00110: Goddard, Shlosman, and Romano-Diaz simulate jetted Seyfert galaxies at high resolution and track them against the major galaxy scaling relations, comparing jet hosts with ordinary galaxies. Jet feedback damps central star formation, pushes gas outward, drives long-lived shocks through interstellar and circumgalactic gas, and trims stellar mass. Jetted Seyferts linger longer in the green valley and reach the quenched region more often, leaving lasting structural, kinematic, and chemical traces despite only transient quenching.
arxiv-2604-00410: Hanada and colleagues offer a one-round, privacy-preserving method for joint medical inference across sites. Pooling summary statistics can still expose patient-level detail when a site holds few patients, because cross-product summaries may reveal covariate patterns for discrete variables. Their method rebuilds the pooled likelihood from site-level summaries for linear mixed models, then adds Gaussian noise to those summaries for site-level differential privacy. Variance estimates that resist clustering, computed straight from the privatised summaries, give valid uncertainty measures.
arxiv-2604-00810: Chaturvedi, El-Gazzar, and van Gerven model how role differentiation can emerge when non-cooperating agents share coupled resource channels under multi-level selection. Group-level selection shapes a shared base and mutation rule. Individuals still face their own selection pressure, in an embodied ecology with positive-sum intake and zero-sum redistribution channels. In their learned ecology, both channels stay occupied at colony level, dodging collapse into a single acquisition mode.
arxiv-2604-01010: Xu, Luo, and Liu introduce Paraphrase-Decomposition-Aggregation, a training-free defense for vision-language models against adversarial image attacks. Earlier methods train against adversarial cases for single tasks, costing much compute and failing on unseen attacks. Their method rewords prompts, splits questions, and merges for match, at test time with no model changes. To balance toughness and speed, they add checks cutting run-time cost while keeping most toughness gains. Tests across models and benchmarks for question answering, sorting, and captions show toughness gains and strong scores.
arxiv-2604-01110: Wyrich and colleagues report on a seminar teaching empirical methods through the hype around AI coding assistants, a topic that drew interest. Hands-on sessions with the assistants were paired with student-designed empirical studies; notes and replies suggest the hype sparked curiosity and critical thinking. Students used the assistants while questioning limits, building the empirical thinking needed to judge claims. Three lessons emerge: hype topics lower barriers to abstract research ideas, hands-on tasks plus ownership of inquiry foster engagement, and one seminar teaches technical and research skills.
arxiv-2604-01210: Mroueh and colleagues present CliffSearch, a search system for discovering scientific algorithms. Each entry is a theory-plus-code item rather than code alone. Language-model agents handle pairing, crossover, mutation and review, with reviewer judgments on being right and newness as hard gates beside benchmark scores. Changes split into novelty-seeking exploration and review-led repair. They test the loop on transformer link evolution, optimizer discovery on a nanoGPT stack, and a native-optimizer test, showing one workflow can steer metrics while keeping finds easy to follow.
arxiv-2604-01310: Nejati Manzari and colleagues present MedQwen, a medical vision-language model built to survive mixed clinical tasks without forgetting earlier ones. They pair a mixture of experts with a scaling rule for low-rank updates matching a full fine-tuned mixture. Each expert starts from a slice of the weights' singular value decomposition, with residual compensation keeping routing stable under distribution shift. Across 23 medical datasets, it nears full fine-tuning on zero-shot classification with 339 times fewer trainable parameters. Forgetting stays near 5 percent where strong baselines lose over 20 to 50 percent.
arxiv-2604-01810: Lee and colleagues study magnetic states in quasi-1D CrSbX3, with X as sulfur or Se, built from double-rutile chains. Standard band theory without Coulomb effects gives band gaps close to experiment. Order proves tied to the chromium-chromium bond length: stretching it flips order from antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic at 3.53 angstrom. CrSbS3 sits near that edge, while CrSbSe3 is ferromagnetic, both matching measured values. Exchange analysis shows the change is driven by a sign flip of intrachain superexchange, while direct exchange stays parallel and shifts slowly.
arxiv-2604-02010: Feng and colleagues sharpen open vocabulary segmentation of remote sensing images with DR-Seg. The task needs language matched recognition and outlines, yet CLIP captures structure poorly. Earlier DINO fixes treat CLIP as one space. DR-Seg splits CLIP features into meaning and structure subspaces, letting DINO strengthen structure without warping meaning. A graph module adds priors to a refined branch, and fusion blends it with the original branch. Tests across eight benchmarks set the state of the art.
arxiv-2604-02310: Singha and colleagues present MeerKAT data on three pulsar binaries in magneto active settings. The high mass binary PSR J1740 3052, the black widow PSR J2051 0827 and the redback PSR J1748 2446A yield polarization, dispersion, rotation and scattering measures. The two eclipsing millisecond pulsars show strong orbital phase linked propagation effects, with two eclipses seen. Smooth rotation shifts in the high mass system pin a small scale magnetic structure in the companion wind.
arxiv-2604-02410: Della Chiesa and colleagues study the double radio relic system in merging cluster MACS J1752.0+4440 with wideband radio data from uGMRT, JVLA and LOFAR. Detailed spectral analysis finds a double peaked brightness and spectral index profile for the brighter northeast relic, including a bright bar substructure, plus surprisingly flat integrated spectral indices for both relics. Spectral curvature maps show two concave spectra, against particle ageing models. The northeast relic properties fit no single shock front scenario; multiple shocks, re-acceleration and projection effects likely shape it.
arxiv-2604-02510: Hartl, Gstöttner and Schöberl present a structurally flat triangular form for control systems with three inputs whose outputs are flat, meaning states and inputs follow from outputs and their derivatives. They define the form through regularity conditions guaranteeing structural flatness, and work out when it matches under static feedback. They also give sufficient conditions for reaching the form after finitely many input prolongations.
arxiv-2604-02810: Cubas Becerra and Crisóstomo Parejas prove every homeomorphism of a compact metric space with a full-support invariant probability measure can be approximated in the C0-Gromov-Hausdorff topology by zero-entropy homeomorphisms. The argument uses ergodic decomposition and dense-orbit points in ergodic components. Topological entropy is thus unstable under such perturbations, and topologically stable maps in this class have dense periodic points.
arxiv-2604-02910: Bohnet and six colleagues test whether large language models reason at their best on planning problems rather than leaning on simple heuristics. In Blocksworld tower tasks and a formally equivalent Path-Star graph task, with depth, width, and compositionality varied, reasoning-enhanced models beat traditional satisficing planners in complex multi-goal settings. Even with semantic hints stripped away, models track theoretical optimality limits almost perfectly.
arxiv-2604-03010: Schwarz and six colleagues measure ionization in the envelopes of three Class 0 protostars, young stars still wrapped in infalling material. It drives physical and chemical evolution, and this early phase shapes later disk chemistry. Using H13CO+ and C18O data from NOEMA and the IRAM 30m, they target NGC-1333 IRAS4A, L1448-C, and L1157. Rates run several orders of magnitude above the diffuse interstellar medium value, supporting stronger ionization-driven chemistry under 100,000 years into evolution.
arxiv-2604-03210: Chiesa and colleagues explain spin selectivity in chiral donor-bridge-acceptor molecules after light excites them, through slow twisting motions. The twists alter hopping and spin-orbit coupling, creating a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction that yields strong spin polarization for realistic settings. Their model also explains the magnetic-field pattern seen in EPR data and predicts a nontrivial temperature pattern.
arxiv-2604-03610: Sun and colleagues introduce DebugHarness, a self-running LLM-powered debugging agent that copies human live debugging for program repair. Driven by a crash that repeats, it forms guesses, probes memory states and run paths, and builds patches through a closed-loop checking cycle. Tested on SEC-bench, a dataset of real C/C++ security flaws, it patches about 90 percent of tested bugs. That is over 30 percent better than state-of-the-art baselines.
arxiv-2604-04110: Jiangdan Li and team measured stellar traits and orbit lengths for 123 hot subdwarf binaries paired with main-sequence stars, drawn from LAMOST low-detail survey data. Subdwarf masses cluster near 0.5 solar masses, as fits stars burning helium in their cores, while companion masses span 0.6 to 1.9 solar masses. Orbit lengths lean long, a pattern the authors tie to how such pairs are picked out rather than to their true spread. The work gives one of the largest catalogs of these pairs, with observational limits on their traits and formation paths.
arxiv-2604-04210: Mustafa S. Abbas and team introduced a joint communication and proactive monitoring system over cell-free massive MIMO. One subset of access points listens to untrusted links, while another serves legitimate users and sends jamming signals toward the untrusted links. This dual role keeps user service reliable while weakening untrusted links and sharpening watch. Closed-form expressions for spectral efficiency and monitoring success were derived under partial zero-forcing precoding with imperfect channel knowledge. A simple access-point mode plan then maximizes watch success under service-quality requirements.
arxiv-2604-04310: Morton and Pavone introduce frax, a JAX library for robot kinematics and dynamics that runs the same Python code on CPU, GPU and TPU. Existing tools tend to favour either CPU speed or GPU throughput. Frax vectorizes robot dynamics fully, enabling fast real-time control, parallel runs and automatic differentiation. On CPU it hits microsecond times fit for kilohertz control, nearing tuned C++ code. On GPU it scales to thousands of instances and over 100 million evaluations per second, validated on a Franka Panda arm and a Unitree G1 humanoid.
arxiv-2604-04410: Takahashi and colleagues propose a stable, consistent way to tune language models to likes. Most tuners assume a likes model, such as Bradley-Terry, which may miss true likes and break consistency. Direct density ratio tuning avoids likes models and reaches consistency, but its ratio often blows up, shaking training. The team's method instead uses a relative ratio between liked data and a mix of liked and unliked data. This relative ratio is capped and never blows up, so training stays stable with tighter bounds than the direct method.
arxiv-2604-04510: Zhao establishes joint extreme values of Dirichlet L-functions and their logarithmic derivatives using the resonance method. Rather than treating each object alone, the paper studies the L-functions and their logarithmic derivatives together, seeking extreme values they attain jointly. The results extend earlier work by Aistleitner and colleagues from 2019 and by Yang from 2023, pushing the resonance method further into the joint setting.
arxiv-2604-04810: Hayes builds a pipeline to hunt for sources that vanish between epochs on digitised Palomar Sky Survey plates. The pipeline spots and filters sources on red plates, refines alignment, and matches across blue and red plates from both epochs, rejecting Pan-STARRS DR1 matches. On a 20-case benchmark it recovers eight of nine sources in the April 1950 field and all three in the July 1952 field, with 0.2 false positives per field. A sweep yields 2.85 million candidates, matching 63.9 percent of a catalog, while a next-day temporal effect proves inconclusive.
arxiv-2604-05010: Mekhontsev shows that the geometric aspect ratio of the Twin Dragon equals one over phi, where phi is the golden ratio. The result follows by solving the covariance fixed-point equation for the self-similar measure, which matches Lebesgue area since the similarity dimension is two. The appearance of phi surprises, because the Twin Dragon is defined purely through the Gaussian integer one plus i, with no pentagonal or Fibonacci structure in its construction.
arxiv-2604-05910: Neamtu, Crisan, and Lang study a two-dimensional vorticity equation on the torus driven by fractional transport noise with Hurst parameter between one half and one. A sewing-lemma variant for transport-type inputs builds the Young integral and opens wider stochastic partial differential equations to study. They prove one solution exists, and it is unique, and derive an estimator for the Hurst value from square terms.
arxiv-2604-06310: Diesing and Metzger model shocks and gamma-ray emission in novae. A white dwarf envelope sheds in an outflow striking a thin older shell. Particles accelerate at the reverse shock, and protons entering the shell radiate calorimetrically, matching optical and gamma-ray emission. Maximum proton energy scales with hot post-shock thickness, capped by turbulent mixing with cooler gas at a ten-thousandth of shock radius, explaining faint X-rays. With that thickness and magnetic amplification, energies reach near 10 GeV at peak, then pass 10 TeV as the shock expands.
arxiv-2604-06410: Henke and twelve others control a quantum dot pair's emission direction in a photonic crystal waveguide with solo wire tuning. The emitters sit 13 microns apart yet remain coupled. A spread dipole-dipole link gives directionality, so the pair forms an artificial molecule. The beam switches left to right with the set driving phase under joint pump. Steady driving yields singles on one port and pairs on the other. Pulsed pump inverts both emitters and yields linked photon pairs. The work shows chiral quantum optics via a non-chiral waveguide.
arxiv-2604-06910: Perinati and three colleagues present and analyze a broken Galerkin method for second-order linear mixed-type partial equations. Such laws change nature from elliptic to hyperbolic across the compute domain. The discrete problem is sound from an energy-norm bound, won through the Morawetz tool. The authors derive hp a priori error bounds in the energy norm, proving closing-in rates for standard and quasi-Trefftz poly spaces. Test runs back the theory results.
arxiv-2604-07010: Vermandere, Bassier, and Vergauwen build a scanning setup in Unity for fake scan sets. Scene rebuild and object finish need sets pairing partial scans with shapes, but real scanning is costly and slow for hidden regions. The system mimics real scanners with detail, range, and noise, using ray scanning for sight and hiding effects. Wide images color the point clouds. An auto maker makes rooms and fittings, and the V-Scan dataset pairs indoor scans with partial point clouds, hiding grids, and complete shapes.
arxiv-2604-07110: Al-Hamdani, Alfè, and Zen weigh whether calcium dotted low dimensional matter can store hydrogen gas well enough for mobile use. Hydrogen tanks of carbon fibre hurt fuel economy, so storing hydrogen stuck on a surface at normal working settings could help. Yet hydrogen binds only weakly in the right energy window, and calcium on graphene tends to form calcium hydride instead. The authors run top grade diffusion Monte Carlo checks beside density models for calcium on boron doped graphene and inside carbon tubes.
arxiv-2604-07510: van Buel, Cichocki, and Everts derive mobility for charged particles in a charged chiral active fluid with odd viscosity. Via the Lorentz reciprocal theorem, applied to odd fluids, they give a general mobility formula under weak electric fields. For a charged sphere at low zeta potentials, they obtain an exact closed-form formula valid for any Debye screening length and odd coefficient. As in Newtonian fluids, motion scales with uncharged-sphere translational motion via the Henry function, but odd viscosity adds directional asymmetries persisting even for thin double layers.
arxiv-2604-07810: Giulio Valentino Dalla Riva and Matteo Dalla Riva introduce Intensity Dot Product Graphs, a latent-position graph model with random node counts. Fixed node sets limit classic models, while graphon designs trade away shape interpretability. Their model swaps fixed latent spots for a Poisson point process on a Euclidean latent space, keeping dot-product links. A population-level rate links smooth latent structure to finite seen graphs. The paper defines smooth analogues of the chance matrix and proves a spectral match for top values.
arxiv-2604-07910: Siris and three colleagues design incentives to cut the carbon emissions of video streaming. Emissions hinge on segment energy use, carbon intensity, and whether users prize quality or green outcomes. Their two-tier subscription pairs a discount with carbon rewards, letting providers drop quality for a capped share of videos per month. The best design sets the lower tier one resolution step below maximum satisfaction. Streaming from a local data center changes how much of the catalog can run at reduced quality.
arxiv-2604-08010: Stenhede gives an algorithm to Legendrian realize a simple closed curve on a Legendrian graph's ribbon surface in standard contact structure. It converts an abstract open book into a contact surgery diagram for the supported manifold. Its monodromy is a product of Dehn twists along nontrivial curves. The paper records a uniqueness claim implicit in earlier work but never stated in the needed form. Any two Legendrian realizations of the same ribbon-surface curve are Legendrian isotopic, as are knots on open-book pages in the same class.
arxiv-2604-08210: Mondal, Mukherjee, and Pramanik prove a higher-dimensional version of a classical theorem: a polygonally cellulated 2-sphere in three-dimensional space, with every vertex of even degree, is 2-face-colourable. To state their result, they introduce combinatorially sphere-like ranked posets, ranked posets that generalize combinatorial spheres. They prove that, in such a poset of rank k, when every element of rank k-2 is covered by evenly many elements, the top-ranked elements admit a proper 2-colouring. Neighbours are coloured differently.
arxiv-2604-08510: Liu and six colleagues argue that language model training follows a hidden lesson plan, with skills emerging in a stable order built from parts. Tracking simple tasks across four model families from 410 million to 13 billion parameters, they find emergence orders strikingly consistent and composite skills usually arriving after their parts. Task similarity inside models also predicts later training paths, suggesting training is more ordered than loss curves show.
arxiv-2604-08710: C.E. Regan and seven colleagues sort solar wind regimes at Mars with unsupervised machine learning on MAVEN spacecraft data spanning solar cycles 24 and 25. Principal component analysis plus K-means clustering on scaled multi dimensional data yields distinct slow, fast, intermediate, and compressed regimes in a physically clear way. Regime counts and timing track solar activity strongly, aiding space physics and future Moon and Mars exploration.
arxiv-2604-08810: Zhou and ten colleagues present R2G, a multi view circuit graph benchmark suite from RTL to GDSII for physical design with graph neural networks. Five stage aware views with information parity span 30 open source IP cores. A DEF to graph pipeline spanning end to end stages, plus loaders, shared splits, domain metrics, and repeatable baselines, complete the suite. Decoupling representation choice from model choice shows view choice dominates model choice. Node centric views generalize best across placement and routing, and decoder head depth of 3 to 4 layers drives accuracy most.
arxiv-2604-08910: Wang and three colleagues present a light, general plan for multi sensor human move spotting from wearable time series. Focus based fusion costs heavily while other methods lack toughness, so the team keeps a split extract fuse pattern with two new ideas. A chained fuse block in place of focus and cross variable fusion through squeeze, loops, join, and fuse. A MixStyle boost module mixes batch means and spreads before time feature stages. Sensor, variable, and channel freedom is kept during splitting, with fast fusion and tough pulling after.
arxiv-2604-09010: Rahaman studies how tungsten isotopes change shape, using covariant density functional theory with four relativistic functionals. The study tracks even-even isotopes from mass 154 to 264, spanning binding energy, quadrupole deformation, two-neutron separation energy, pairing energy, radii, and potential energy curves. Results trace shape changes and stability from neutron-poor to neutron-rich isotopes. Matches with deformed Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov, droplet model, and relativistic mean field work support the method. The findings bear on rapid neutron-capture element building and tests at radioactive ion beam facilities.
arxiv-2604-09210: Shukla, Remondino, and Risse tackle depth loss when animals are filmed with one camera, where detection gives flat boxes with no facing hint. Their pipeline fits skinned multi-animal body models to estimate three-dimensional boxes, then projects them into image space as labels with a refined camera pose method. Cuboid face visibility metrics show which side of the animal the camera caught. Tests on the Animal3D set show accurate results across species and settings, a step toward monocular 3D animal detection.
arxiv-2604-09310: Martin and colleagues investigate precise control of tiny nuclear spin groups in the spin noise regime using diamond defects. Active spin control via radio waves is often unnecessary for standard detection but becomes essential for advanced NMR protocols. Using correlation methods, they show spin dynamics depend critically on the initial radio phase and its angle to the crystal axis. Depending on those parameters, identical nuclear rotations can yield full, partial, or no contrast in readout, so imperfect calibration can cause unclear signals and misreading of spin dynamics.
arxiv-2604-09510: Makarieva and five colleagues rethink how added vegetation affects water supplies, using China's vast restoration effort as their test case. They contend that methods ignoring how plants reshape atmospheric circulation are built to find harm to streamflow, since rainfall responds nonlinearly to airborne moisture. Falling flows in dry regions, they suggest, mark early succession rather than a lasting loss, and mature ecosystems may instead raise water availability.
arxiv-2604-09910: Telesca, Marco, and Landry extend mixed-group models, where each case partly belongs to several pure classes, to layered curve data. They translate the standard multi-way Karhunen-Loeve breakdown into a simple layered model for usable, loose random processes. A layered pushing prior on the unitary simplex aids finding of partial group structures. The work is driven and shown by brain-wave studies of children with autism spectrum disorder.
arxiv-2604-10010: Kapustyan, Martynyuk, Misiats, and Stanzhytskyi study the long-run behavior of a stochastic thin-film equation. It adds linear fixed and random Ito terms. They prove nonnegative weak martingale solutions exist for all time from zero onward. In square mean, the peak value settles toward the space average of the start. That average is times a random factor like a geometric Wiener process.
arxiv-2604-10210: Qin and five colleagues propose A3-FPN, a pyramid network for dense tasks that handles object scale shifts. Current pyramid networks miss telling cues and small objects. A3-FPN uses a disentangled design with content-aware focus and a spread column network for global exchange across levels. Fusion gathers nearby content for spot-wise offsets and weights in context-aware sampling. On COCO and Cityscapes, A3-FPN joins leading CNN and transformer models, scoring 49.6 mask AP on COCO and about 86 mean overlap over union there.
arxiv-2604-10410: Srivastava, Bhosale, Doermann, and Gao sharpen machine written chest X-ray reports. Single pass writing lets word habits crowd out image cues, spawning false linked findings. Their CWCD method writes one report per disease group, pitting plain scans against masked scans. Group wise visual cues steer each draft, cutting the drift toward stock phrases. Tests beat base methods on both clinical value and plain language scores.
arxiv-2604-10510: Hu, Meng, and Tang solve a backward stochastic control problem in discrete time. Their linear quadratic system runs backward from a terminal rule, unlike forward systems. In a Hilbert space frame, they pin down when the problem can be solved at all. A backward maximum rule yields the Hamiltonian system for the best control. Decoupling then gives a Riccati equation plus a direct state feedback law.
arxiv-2604-10810: Jabłoński and three colleagues investigate nth roots of bounded operators in the conditionally positive definite class. Main result: if T is CPD and its nth power is subnormal, quasinormal, normal, or a 3-isometry, then T is in that class. This shows these classes are invariant under nth roots in the CPD class, as in earlier results. They further characterize quasinormal and normal operators via their CPD property and triplet. By theory and explicit examples, they show CPD and normaloid operators are distinct classes.
arxiv-2604-11310: Traianou and nine colleagues report an orphan gamma-ray flare from the radio galaxy 3C 120 during its brightest outburst in March 2018, recently linked to an IceCube neutrino alert. Despite gamma-ray power near 3.7 times ten to the 44 ergs per second, X-ray, optical, and radio monitoring showed no matching variability. VLBI imaging traced a new jet disturbance crossing a stationary feature and compressing the magnetic field. The Ring of Fire model, in which the disturbance scatters photons from that feature, reproduces the flare.
arxiv-2604-11510: Yao and four colleagues split a language model's policy into two modes to spur wider exploration without losing accuracy. A normal mode aims at correct answers, while a high-entropy mode favors exploration, and the two learn together under shared parameters. Tests across model sizes show the split beats standard entropy-guided baselines on general and creative tasks. The high-entropy mode yields distinct behavior patterns that supply fresh learning signals.
arxiv-2604-12010: Hernández bounds the norm of the Schwarzian derivative for convex holomorphic mappings on the polydisk and the unit ball in complex n-space. For coordinate-wise convex mappings on the polydisk, he derives a sharp estimate extending the classical one-variable result of Chuaqui, Duren, and Osgood to higher dimensions. For the Roper-Suffridge extension operator in the unit ball, he obtains an explicit bound, the best available estimate in that setting.
arxiv-2604-12310: Mitsuno and three colleagues build a dialogue agent that shares everyday information between older adults and their grandchildren to fight social isolation. The agent chats daily with both sides on a chatbot platform, passing along what each side shares to deepen engagement and family connection. In a ten-day trial with 52 grandparent-grandchild pairs, older adults grew more willing to interact. Grandparent-grandchild bonds strengthened, and daily chats were linked to lower anxiety on both sides.
arxiv-2604-12410: Krzysztof Urbanowski studies the math behind quantum uncertainty relations. He treats the Schwarz inequality and inequalities drawn from Jensen's inequality. Those tools yield Heisenberg-Robertson and Schrödinger-Robertson rules for pairs that do not commute. He extends them to three or more at once and probes their edge cases. Sum rules follow from Jensen's inequality as well. He also links the broadened rules to correlations in a given state. Pearson-style coefficients give a matching form of the Schrödinger-Robertson rule.
arxiv-2604-12910: Gilles Cohen-Tannoudji and three colleagues model dark matter as a gluonic condensate. Guided by the galactic acceleration scale, it forms a rigid structure with a protected gap. Lorentz covariance and unitarity favor the AdS algebra so(2,3). The condensate yields a cored halo of finite mass. Normalizing by surface density gives acceleration near 1.9 times ten to the minus ten meters per second squared. That value sits inside the empirical range. SPARC rotation curves fit the profile broadly, though no precision fit is claimed.
arxiv-2604-13010: Wu, Han, and Cai remove the live teacher server from on-policy distillation, a costly requirement of training large reasoning models. They trace naive offline attempts to a broken condition they call teacher consistency, the same teacher serving both fine-tuning and distillation, and build Lightning OPD around it. The method matches standard distillation while training four times faster, reaching 69.9 percent on AIME 2024 from a Qwen3-8B base in 30 GPU hours.
arxiv-2604-13110: Ván and Somogyfoki reverse a recent claim that the Second Law fails to ensure stability in third-order non-Fourier heat conduction. The earlier analysis found a stability rule it could not derive from standard thermodynamic inequalities. The authors show a more careful proof closes the gap: concave entropy and non-negative entropy production do suffice. The key point is that every coefficient of the dispersion polynomial stays positive for all physical wave numbers, ruling out positive real roots.
arxiv-2604-13510: Mukherjee and Ali carry Lie's theorem into supertropical algebra. Lie's theorem is a classic result about solvable Lie algebras, and their version carries that result into the supertropical setting, where addition and multiplication follow tropical rules. The paper's aim is that single extension, giving supertropical algebra a Lie-theoretic tool that mirrors the classical case. Its contribution is the proof itself, stated for the supertropical framework and extending Lie theory to a new algebraic setting.
arxiv-2604-13810: Zhou extends hidden zeros and 2-splits from tree-level Tr(phi-cubed) amplitudes to loop-level Feynman integrands, setting aside scaleless integrals. The key is a factorization mechanism in Feynman diagrams under shuffle sums. Loop-level zeros and splits differ from the literature's, yet their kinematic conditions are simple. The zero-to-split link is as tight as at tree level, via the same procedure. The loop-level 2-split formula generalizes the tree one: an L-loop integrand becomes a sum over L-plus-one terms, each with 2-split structure.
arxiv-2604-14210: Ren and colleagues test the circulating claim that Chinese prompts beat English on token efficiency for vibe coding, a claim tied to savings up to 40 percent. On SWE-bench Lite, the Chinese advantage fails to appear. Token costs swing by model: MiniMax-2.7 runs about 1.28 times costlier in Chinese, while GLM-5 runs cheaper. Success rates in Chinese trail English across every model tested, so the authors warn practitioners not to expect savings or gains from switching languages.
arxiv-2604-14310: González and two colleagues derive a lower bound on transport effort for dynamic soaring from a simplified optimal-control model. Slow flight pays a drag penalty, fast flight a dissipative penalty, and wind shear grants an energetic subsidy. Rescaling four species to baselines, they place all on one reduced speed-effort plane and calibrate the bound to the wandering albatross. Two more dynamic soarers sit progressively above the bound, while the thermal-soaring crane sits about 33 times farther from it. Nearness to the bound measures wind-powered transport.
arxiv-2604-15010: Jacopin introduces prolepsis: a transformer commits early, task-specific heads sustain it, and no layer corrects it. Replicating a planning-site finding on Gemma 2 2B and Llama 3.2 1B, he tests five questions. Planning proves invisible to six residual-stream methods, and a spike replicates at the final prompt token. Specific heads route the decision to the output, and evidence fits search within 16 layers plus commitment beyond. Factual recall shows the same motif at a different depth, with no overlap between planning heads and the factual top-10.
arxiv-2604-15110: Zhang and Chen find all exact static solutions of the source-free SU(2) Yang-Mills equations where the gauge potential depends on spin operators. A vector-potential extraction method yields the most general spin vector potential, set by three constants and two radial functions. Solving the resulting consistency equations gives a full classification across real and complex families, with the known simple case falling out as a special case.
arxiv-2604-15210: Vural and colleagues teach machines to reason about cartoon humor the way expert captionists do. Their IRS framework splits the job into spotting visual mismatches, building coherent reinterpretations, and ranking candidates against human judgments. Structured traces make the path from perception to punchline explicit and learnable. Across three model sizes on the New Yorker contest, IRS-72B tops ranking at 76.1 percent, beating non-expert humans and all tested multimodal baselines, and transfers zero-shot to new cases.
arxiv-2604-15310: Chaturvedi and seven colleagues present TokenLight, a method for relighting photos with precise, continuous control over several lighting traits at once. Attribute tokens encode intensity, color, ambient light, diffuse level, and 3D light positions, and the model trains mostly on synthetic data with true lighting labels plus some real photos. It leads prior work on tests and handles hard cases such as lights inside objects and see-through materials.
arxiv-2604-15510: Kos, Wild, and Nielsen find strong nonergodic behavior in coupled-chain XX models, where domain-wall starts keep a lumpy magnetization pattern for arbitrarily long times. The cause is zero modes guarded by chiral symmetry, and Lanczos study points to a localization transition at a critical coupling between chains. Antiferromagnetic defects and symmetry-breaking perturbations restore slow thermalization, while symmetry-preserving ones leave the effect intact.
